title: Later influences: Hines, Stacy, Wilson, Waller, Tatum
summary: Hines most revolutionized his style, followed by Stacy, Wilson, Waller and Tatum.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Well, certainly your piano style goes beyond the ragtime realm. What have any other pianists of the swing era or the modern era influence your playing as it's constituted today?

I think that the first real impact that hit me, when I say impact, I was already going under the influence of the old timers like Jelly Roll and the ragtime pianists. And I had one pianist around here by the name of Buzzy Williams, who was very, very excellent, and he gave me a lot of encouragement and a lot of help. But getting back to the other pianists, I would say that the first one that really had a terrific impact on me was Earl Hines. I think that he did more to revolutionize my style of playing probably than any other pianist that I know of. And then came Jess Stacy, who played in the big band with Goodman, and of course Teddy Wilson, who I think was simply superb. And of course then I wouldn't leave out good old Fats Wally. Fats had a terrific influence on me too in those days. And I see these pianists began to have an influence on me, but it was only after I had been playing for many years.
Did you take up, were you taken up much by Art Tatum's style?
Very much. Oh yes, yes, definitely with Art Tatum. I was definitely taken up with him. I first heard him I think around 36 or 37, something like that.
